verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「要吩咐以色列人，把那为点灯捣成的清橄榄油拿来给你，使灯常常点着。
verses.en: “Command the Israelites to bring[NOTE:1] to you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and let them take.” The simple vav (ו) on the imperfect/jussive form of the verb לָקַח (laqakh, “to take”) following the imperative (“Command”) indicates a purpose clause (“to bring…”).
Heb “to cause to ascend a lamp continually.”
verses.commentary:
24:2 "Command the sons of Israel" This IMPERATIVE (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel) is
unusual in Leviticus. Many chapters are introduced by "speak" (BDB 180, KB 210, Piel IMPERATIVE)
but only here, "command."

▣

NASB, JPSOA, REB
"clear"

NKJV, NRSV, TEV, LXX, Peshitta
"pure"

NJB
"crushed"

The MT has the MASCULINE ADJECTIVE "pure" (BDB 269), the
VERB form means "be bright," "clear," or "pure." The ADJECTIVE denotes that
which is "free from foreign substances" (cf. Exod. 27:20-21; Lev. 24:7). The special olive oil (see James Freeman,
Manners and Customs of the Bible, p. 74) was to be used in the inner shrine (holy place) and, therefore, must
be uncontaminated.

The same ADJECTIVE (but FEMININE) is used in Lev. 24:4 to
describe the metal of the lampstand (gold, cf. Exod. 25:31,39; 31:8; 37:17).

The same ADJECTIVE is used in Lev. 24:6 for the gold table on which the Show Bread
rested in the Holy Place (cf. Exod. 25:23-30; 31:8; 37:11).

The same ADJECTIVE is used in Lev. 24:7 of the additive to the frankincense on the
Show Bread (cf. Exod. 30:34).

▣ "the light" It is mentioned in Exod. 25:6; 27:20; 35:14,28; 39:37; Num. 4:9,16. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAMPSTAND (Menorah).

There are several words in this context used to describe this lamp of the Holy Place.

- Lev. 24:2, "luminary" (BDB 22, cf. Exod. 35:14,28; 39:37)

- Lev. 24:2, "lamp" (BDB 632, cf. Lev. 24:4)

- Lev. 24:4, "lampstand" (BDB 633)

All three are mentioned in Exod. 39:37. It was one lampstand with seven flower shaped bowls on the top
of branches.

▣ "burn continuously" This is a recurrent demand, cf. Lev. 24:3 (thrice), 4, 8 (twice). This means from
evening to morning, not all day (cf. Exod. 27:20-21).

verses.zh: 在会幕中法柜的幔子外，亚伦从晚上到早晨必在耶和华面前经理这灯。这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。
verses.en: Outside the special curtain[NOTE:1] of the congregation in the Meeting Tent, Aaron[NOTE:2] must arrange it from evening until morning before the Lord continually. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew term פָּרֹכֶת (parokhet) is usually translated “veil” or “curtain.” It seems to have stretched not only in front of but also over the top of the ark of the covenant which stood behind and under it inside the most holy place thus forming a canopy (see R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 3:687-89).
Several medieval Hebrew mss, Smr, and the LXX add “and his sons.”
Heb “for your generations.”
verses.commentary:
24:3 "the veil of testimony" This refers to the inner veil which divided the "holy of Holies" (where the ark
was located) from the "holy place," where the special furniture was located (see
SPECIAL TOPIC:
TABERNACLE (chart), cf. Lev. 4:6).

The ark was known as the "ark of testimony" (cf. Exod. 25:22) so the veil before it took this designation.

▣ "it shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations" This phrase is made up of three parallel parts.

- ADVERB, "continually" (BDB 556, i.e., in the night time, every night, cf. Exod. 30:7,8)

- NOUN, "'olam" (BDB 761, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER)

- phrase, "throughout your generations" (cf. Lev. 7:36; 10:P9; 23:41)

Remember, in the OT "forever" must be interpreted in context. Most of YHWH's covenant promises are
conditional on obedience (see NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 348-349). Also note that the OT was a "guardian" only for a period
of time (i.e., cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; Hebrews; and
SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW).

verses.zh: 他要在耶和华面前常收拾精金灯台上的灯。」
verses.en: On the ceremonially pure lampstand[NOTE:1] he must arrange the lamps before the Lord continually.
notes: Alternatively, “pure [gold] lampstand,” based on Exod 25:31, etc., where the term for “gold” actually appears (see NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT, and the remarks in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 395, etc.). However, in Lev 24:4 the adjective “pure” is feminine, corresponding to “lampstand,” not an assumed noun “gold” (contrast Exod 25:31), and the “table” in v. 6 was overlaid with gold, but was not made of pure gold. Therefore, it is probably better to translate “[ceremonially] pure lampstand” (v. 4) and “[ceremonially] pure table” (v. 6); see NEB; cf. KJV, ASV; B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 164-65; and G. J. Wenham, Leviticus [NICOT], 307.

verses.zh: 「你要取细面，烤成十二个饼，每饼用面伊法十分之二。
verses.en: “You must take choice wheat flour[NOTE:1] and bake twelve loaves;[NOTE:2] there must be two-tenths of an ephah of flour in[NOTE:3] each loaf,
notes: See the note on Lev 2:1.
Heb “and bake it twelve loaves”; KJV, NAB, NASB “cakes.”
See the note on Lev 5:11. tn The words “of flour” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
24:5 "fine flour" This refers to wheat flour not barley flour.

▣ "twelve cakes" They may have symbolized

- a previous covenant (Noah, Abraham)

- an everlasting covenant

- the twelve tribes

- YHWH providing Israel's physical needs

See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE.

▣ "ephah" This term is assumed. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES.

verses.zh: 要把饼摆列两行（或译：摞；下同），每行六个，在耶和华面前精金的桌子上；
verses.en: and you must set them in two rows, six in a row,[NOTE:1] on the ceremonially pure table before the Lord.
notes: Heb “six of the row.”
verses.commentary:
24:6 "you shall set them in rows" These were large loaves (Lev. 24:5, about � 3.5 lbs.) and they were
arranged on a small table. Josephus (Antiq. 3.6.6) says they were piled up on top of each other.

▣ "the pure gold table before the Lord" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SHOW BREAD OF THE PRESENCE.

The phrase "before the Lord" denoted in the Tabernacle's holy shrine.

verses.zh: 又要把净乳香放在每行饼上，作为纪念，就是作为火祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: You must put pure frankincense[NOTE:1] on each row,[NOTE:2] and it will become a memorial portion[NOTE:3] for the bread, a gift[NOTE:4] to the Lord.
notes: This is not just any “incense” (קְטֹרֶת, qetoret; R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 3:913-16), but specifically “frankincense” (לְבֹנָה, levonah; R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 2:756-57).

Heb “on [עַל, ʿal] the row,” probably used distributively, “on each row” (J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 395-96). Perhaps the frankincense was placed “with” or “along side of” each row, not actually on the bread itself, and was actually burned as incense to the Lord (cf. NIV84 “Along [Alongside CEV] each row”; NIV11 “by each stack”; NRSV “with each row”; NLT “near each row”; B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 165). This particular preposition can have such a meaning.

The “memorial portion” (אַזְכָרָה, ʾazkharah) was normally the part of the grain offering that was burnt on the altar (see Lev 2:2 and the notes there), as opposed to the remainder, which was normally consumed by the priests (Lev 2:3; see the full regulations in Lev 6:14-23 [6:7-16 HT]).
See the note on Lev 1:9 regarding the term “gift.”
verses.commentary:
24:7 "frankincense" Apparently it was burned beside the bread. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FRANKINCENSE.

▣ "a memorial portion" This refers to part of the offering burned on the altar to YHWH (cf. Lev. 2:2,9,16).

Here it refers to the frankincense (cf. Lev. 2:1,2,14-16; 6:15).

verses.zh: 每安息日要常摆在耶和华面前；这为以色列人作永远的约。
verses.en: Each Sabbath day[NOTE:1] Aaron[NOTE:2] must arrange it before the Lord continually; this portion[NOTE:3] is from the Israelites as a perpetual covenant.
notes: Heb “In the day of the Sabbath, in the day of the Sabbath.” The repetition is distributive. A few medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, and the Syriac delete the second occurrence of the expression.
Heb “he”; the referent (Aaron) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The word “portion” is supplied in the translation here for clarity, to specify what “this” refers to.
verses.commentary:
24:8 See notes at Lev. 24:3. For "sabbath day" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT) and
SABBATH (NT). For "everlasting" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam).
For "covenant" see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

verses.zh: 这饼是要给亚伦和他子孙的；他们要在圣处吃，为永远的定例，因为在献给耶和华的火祭中是至圣的。」
verses.en: It will belong to Aaron and his sons, and they must eat it in a holy place because it is most holy to him, a perpetually-allotted portion[NOTE:1] from the gifts of the Lord.”
notes: Or “a perpetual regulation”; NRSV “a perpetual due.”
verses.commentary:
24:9 The priests were to eat the week old bread (i.e., a type of grain offering accompanied by an incense
offering). It was "most holy" because part of it was offered by fire to YHWH on the altar of sacrifice and was then taken
into the Tabernacle's "holy place."

Although the text does not specifically mention that it was made from unleavened bread, the time
element involved in its consumption by the priests strongly implies this.

verses.zh: 有一个以色列妇人的儿子，他父亲是埃及人，一日闲游在以色列人中。这以色列妇人的儿子和一个以色列人在营里争斗。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] an Israelite woman’s son whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites, and the Israelite woman’s son and an Israelite man[NOTE:2] had a fight in the camp.
notes: Heb “And.”
Heb “the Israelite man,” but Smr has no article, and the point is that there was a conflict between the man of mixed background and a man of full Israelite descent.
verses.commentary:
24:10-23 This is a very detailed historical account, it is only one of two historical accounts in Leviticus; the
other being Leviticus 10 (i.e., the death of Nadab and Abihu). Several items to notice:

- If the mother was Israeli the children were considered Israelite. There were many half Egyptians with Israel.

- Israelis still sinned

- the fight (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 137)

- the blasphemy (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 828-830)

- The tribe of Dan is always depicted as a problem because they left their tribal allotment (cf. Judges 18).

verses.zh: 这以色列妇人的儿子亵渎了圣名，并且咒诅，就有人把他送到摩西那里。（他母亲名叫示罗密，是但支派底伯利的女儿。）
verses.en: The Israelite woman’s son misused the Name and cursed,[NOTE:1] so they brought him to Moses. (Now his mother’s name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
notes: The verb rendered “misused” means literally “to bore through, to pierce” (HALOT 719 s.v. נקב qal); it is from נָקַב (naqav), not קָבַב (qavav; see the participial form in v. 16a). Its exact meaning here is uncertain. The two verbs together may form a hendiadys, “he pronounced by cursing blasphemously” (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 166), the idea being one of the following: (1) he pronounced the name “Yahweh” in a way or with words that amounted to “some sort of verbal aggression against Yahweh himself” (E. S. Gerstenberger, Leviticus [OTL], 362), (2) he pronounced a curse against the man using the name “Yahweh” (N. H. Snaith, Leviticus and Numbers [NCBC], 110; G. J. Wenham, Leviticus [NICOT], 311), or (3) he pronounced the name “Yahweh” and thereby blasphemed, since the “Name” was never to be pronounced (a standard Jewish explanation). In one way or another, the offense surely violated Exod 20:7, one of the ten commandments, and the same verb for cursing is used explicitly in Exod 22:28 (27 HT) for prohibition against “cursing” God. For a full discussion of these and related options for interpreting this verse see P. J. Budd, Leviticus (NCBC), 335-36; J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 408-9; and Levine, 166.
verses.commentary:
24:11 "blasphemed" This VERB (BDB 866 II, KB 1060, cf. Lev. 24:15) means "to utter a curse
against someone," here using YHWH's holy name (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH).

▣ "cursed" This VERB (BDB 886, KB 1103, cf. Lev. 24:14,15; 19:14; 20:9; cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3,
pp.924-927 and 860) is parallel to "blasphemed."

NIV has "blasphemed with a curse," which expresses the thought well.

NJB has "blasphemed the name and cursed it," which is also possible. It was a spoken disrespect to
YHWH (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 149-150).

verses.zh: 他们把那人收在监里，要得耶和华所指示的话。
verses.en: So they placed him in custody until they were able[NOTE:1] to make a clear legal decision for themselves based on words from the mouth of the Lord.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “until they were able” are not in the Hebrew text, but are implied.

The Hebrew here is awkward. A literal reading would be something like the following: “And they placed him in custody to give a clear decision [HALOT 976 s.v. פרשׁ qal] for themselves on the mouth of the Lord.” In any case, they were apparently waiting for a direct word from the Lord regarding this matter (see vv. 13ff).
verses.commentary:
24:12 The priests needed YHWH to make His will clearly known, possibly using

- Urim and Thummin (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM)

- dream (like Jacob)

- prophet (later way to know YHWH's will); see

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「把那咒诅圣名的人带到营外。叫听见的人都放手在他头上；全会众就要用石头打死他。
verses.en: “Bring the one who cursed outside the camp, and all who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation is to stone him to death.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “to death” are supplied in the translation as a clarification; they are clearly implied from v. 16.
verses.commentary:
24:14 Notice the procedure.

- Take the offender outside the camp (i.e., away from the holy Tabernacle and covenant people).

- All who heard lay their hands on his head. This was either

- a transfer of guilt (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAYING ON OF HANDS)

- a gesture similar to court witnessing (i.e., identifying the offender, cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1016, #1)

- Let all the congregation stone him (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1050). This was a designated way to remove an offender
from the covenant people (cf. Deut. 17:2-7; 21:18-21).

verses.zh: 你要晓谕以色列人说：凡咒诅　神的，必担当他的罪。
verses.en: Moreover,[NOTE:1] you are to tell the Israelites, ‘If any man curses his God,[NOTE:2] he will bear responsibility for his sin,
notes: Heb “And.”
See the note on v. 11 above and esp. Exod 22:28 [27 HT].
verses.commentary:
24:15 "then he will bear his sin" This is an idiom of death and guilt (cf. Lev. 5:1; 20:20; Num. 9:13; 18:22),
whether by man or God is often not specified.

verses.zh: 那亵渎耶和华名的，必被治死；全会众总要用石头打死他。不管是寄居的是本地人，他亵渎耶和华名的时候，必被治死。
verses.en: and one who misuses[NOTE:1] the name of the Lord must surely be put to death. The whole congregation must surely stone him, whether he is a resident foreigner or a native citizen; when he misuses the Name he must be put to death.
notes: See the note on v. 11 above.
verses.commentary:
24:16 "shall surely be put to death" This is an intensified grammatical form (i.e., an
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of the same root; here BDB 559,
KB 562, repeated in Lev. 24:17).

▣ "shall certainly stone him" This is the same kind of intensified form as above, here BDB 920, KB 1187.

Death was the mandated penalty and stoning by the whole community was the mandated form.

Note the penalty is carried out in Lev. 24:23.

verses.zh: 打死人的，必被治死；
verses.en: “‘If a man beats any person to death,[NOTE:1] he must be put to death.
notes: Heb “And if a man strikes any soul [נֶפֶשׁ, nefesh] of mankind.” The idiom seems to derive from the idea of striking a fatal blow to the very “life” (literally, “soul”) of a human being, not just landing a blow on their body (HALOT 698 s.v. נכה hif.2). On the difficulty of the meaning and significance of the term נֶפֶשׁ see the notes on Lev 17:10-11.
verses.commentary:
24:17 "If a man" The judgment of YHWH on this blasphemer was meant to set a precedent (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE, B. #1).
Notice the "ifs" in Lev. 24:15,17,19.

▣

NASB
"takes the life"

NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"kills"

TEV
"commit murder"

NJB
"strikes down"

REB, LXX
"strikes"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 645, KB 697, Hiphil IMPERFECT)
which can denote

- one fatal blow ‒ here

- one non-fatal blow ‒ Num. 22:23,25,27

- beat repeatedly ‒ Exod. 2:11,13; 5:10

- metaphor

- of sun ‒ Ps. 121:6; Isa. 49:10; Jonah 4:8

- of tongue ‒ Jer. 18:18

verses.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜，以命偿命。
verses.en: One who beats an animal to death[NOTE:1] must make restitution for it, life for life.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And one who strikes a soul of an animal.”
Heb “soul under soul.” Cf. KJV “beast for beast”; NCV “must give…another animal to take its place.”
verses.commentary:
24:18 See notes at Lev. 5:16; 6:5; 22:14; 24:21.

▣ "life for life" This is the term nephesh, twice. See full note at Ezek. 18:4.

verses.zh: 人若使他邻舍的身体有残疾，他怎样行，也要照样向他行：
verses.en: If a man inflicts an injury on[NOTE:1] his fellow citizen,[NOTE:2] just as he has done it must be done to him—
notes: Heb “gives a flaw in”; KJV, ASV “cause a blemish in.”
Or “neighbor” (so NAB, NASB, NIV); TEV, NLT “another person.”
verses.commentary:
24:19-20 This was the Israeli's way (i.e., Lex Talionis, cf. Exod. 21:22-25; see Hard Sayings of the Bible,
pp. 150-151) to limit violence and tribal warfare. The family had the right of limited retaliation (i.e., the kinsman avenger,
cf. Joshua 20-21).

Later the rabbis allowed a price to be paid for some injuries which violated this text and Deut. 19:21.

According to Gordon Wenham, Leviticus, New International Commentary, p. 312, verses
16-22 form a chiasm, with vv. 19-20 being the main truth. Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 149-150, explains how
the rabbis developed the idea of appropriate compensation. However, for premeditated murder there was no compensation
(i.e., Num. 35:31; Deut. 19:11-12).

24:19

NASB, TEV, NJB
"injures"

NKJV
"causes disfigurement"

NRSV, JPSOA
"maims"

REB
"injures and disfigures"

LXX, Peshitta
"give a blemish"

The MT has BDB 548, which can refer to

- physical blemish or defect ‒ Lev. 21:17,18,21,23

- moral blemish ‒ Deut. 32:5

A general translation, REB, is able to cover the semantic range.

verses.zh: 以伤还伤，以眼还眼，以牙还牙。他怎样叫人的身体有残疾，也要照样向他行。
verses.en: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth—just as he inflicts an injury on another person[NOTE:1] that same injury[NOTE:2] must be inflicted on him.
notes: Heb “in the man [אָדָם, ʾadam].”
Heb “just as he inflicts an injury…it must be inflicted on him.” The referent (“that same injury”) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜；打死人的，必被治死。
verses.en: One who beats an animal to death[NOTE:1] must make restitution for it, but[NOTE:2] one who beats a person to death must be put to death.
notes: See the note on v. 18 above.
Heb “and,” but here the Hebrew conjunction ו (vav, “and”) is adversative, contrasting the consequences of beating an animal to death with those of beating a person to death.

verses.zh: 不管是寄居的是本地人，同归一例。我是耶和华―你们的　神。」
verses.en: There will be one regulation[NOTE:1] for you, whether a resident foreigner[NOTE:2] or a native citizen, for I am the Lord your God.’”
notes: Heb “a regulation of one”; KJV, ASV “one manner of law”; NASB “one standard.”

On the Hebrew גֵּר (ger, “resident foreigner”) see notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11. Several passages emphasize equal standing under Mosaic Law (Exod 12:49; Lev 24:22; Num 9:14; 15:15, 16, 26, 29; 19:10; 35:15; Deut 1:16) or similar obligations (Exod 20:10; 23:12; Lev 16:29; 17:10, 12, 13; 18:26; 24:16; Num 15:14).
verses.commentary:
24:22 YHWH is no respecter of persons. There is one justice for all; men, women, Israelite, stranger
(cf. Exod. 12:49; Num. 9:14;15:15,16,29; Deuteronomy especially mentions the widow, orphan, and alien; see
NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 588, #3, [b]).

Remember, a "mixed multitude" came out of Egypt (cf. Exod. 12:38). This would have included

- some other foreign slaves

- some half-Egyptian families

- some Israelite supporters who were expelled

▣ "I am the Lord your God" This is a recurrent covenant form used in
Leviticus 18-26.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is the IMPERATIVE ("command") of Lev. 24:2 different from the normal introductory
IMPERATIVE, "speak"?

- List the different names used for the light in the Holy Place.

- Explain the range of meaning of "perpetual."

- What did the twelve loaves of bread symbolize?

- How is Lev. 24:10-23 different from the rest of the surrounding material?

- Is there a distinction between "blaspheme" and "curse"?

- Why did the hearers of the cursing lay their hands on the head of the person to be stoned?

- How does this chapter express the differing consequences between the death of a human and an animal?

- Explain the significance of Lev. 24:22.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Care for the Menorah (Lev. 24:1-4)

- This information is also found in Exod. 27:20-21.

- This lampstand is described in Exod. 25:31-40. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAMPSTAND (Menorah).

- Care for the Table of Show Bread (Lev. 24:5-9)

- This information is also found in Exod. 25:23-30; 37:10-16; 40:22-23; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHOW BREAD or BREAD OF THE PRESENCE.

- The bread had to be made of precise ingredients and was replaced every week.

- The old bread was to be eaten by the priests (Lev. 24:9).

- A case of blasphemy (Lev. 24:10-12) and how to handle it (Lev. 24:13-16). Punishment meted out in Lev. 24:23.

- Notice the "ifs" (Lev. 24:15,17,19). Specific acts require special punishments.

- cursing God ‒ stoning to death

- murder ‒ death penalty

- death of an animal ‒ restitution

- injury to a neighbor ‒ same to the offender (i.e., eye-for-eye, Lev. 24:20)

- one standard of justice shall apply to all levels of Israeli society (Lev. 24:22)
